subject: history
title: Causes and Consequences 1066-1750
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace cause and effect — why these big events happened and what they changed.
meta_desc: GCSE History Medieval & Early Modern causes and consequences — feudalism, plague, Reformation and civil war.
final_note: You can now explain the chain of cause and effect from Norman rule to the English Civil War.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Black Death changed everything.

With fewer workers, peasants wanted higher wages. Lords resisted. Then a new poll tax in 1381 sparked the Peasants' Revolt, led by Wat Tyler.

It failed — but lords could not turn back the clock on wages.

Henry VIII wanted a male heir and a divorce from Catherine of Aragon — the Pope refused.

Henry made himself Head of the Church of England with the Act of Supremacy in 1534. He then dissolved the monasteries and seized their wealth.

Charles I clashed with Parliament over money, religion and his belief in divine right.

When he tried to arrest five MPs in 1642, war began. By 1649 Parliament had him executed — a king killed by his own people.

The Reformation
The Norman Conquest

options: He wanted a Protestant Bible only
The Pope refused his divorce
He invaded France
Parliament forced him to

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.

mcqs.q: What caused the First World War?
options: Long-term tensions (militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism) combined with the July Crisis triggered by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
The Black Death was caused by witches and was stopped by burning them.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand caused the war.
Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.

mcqs.q: What were the long-term effects of the Black Death?
options: The Black Death was caused by witches and was stopped by burning them.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
Labour shortages strengthened peasants' bargaining power, weakened serfdom in England, contributed to the Peasants' Revolt, and reshaped religious authority.
The Black Death wiped out medieval society and ended the Middle Ages overnight.
